question.problem:
Consider the matrix 
$T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & -7 & 2 \\ -9 & 17 & -10\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
In order to find a basis of $\text{Col}(T),$ we reduce the matrix $T$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & -7 & 2 \\ -9 & 17 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 \\ -9 & 17 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+9{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns, while the $3$rd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one. 

The $1$st and $2$nd columns from the original matrix are ${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $\text{Col}(T)$ is $\{{t}_{1},{t}_{2}\},$ that is to say, 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -9\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -7 \\ 17\end{aligned}]\}.
$$
